frames.slice_level: Upper thorax, at or just above the aortic arch (approximately T2-T4). Trachea round and midline; no arch contour resolved.
Carina / proximal main bronchi, approximately T5-T6. Airway seen centrally as a transverse lucency at the bifurcation.
Below the carina, at the main bronchi / bronchus intermedius, approximately T6-T7. Both bronchi visible as paired lucencies within the mediastinum.

cases.impression: Three contiguous axial levels of an unenhanced chest CT — upper thorax, carina, and main bronchi — all technically unremarkable on soft-tissue window. Lungs are well aerated bilaterally and extend to the chest wall on every frame, with branching pulmonary vessels that become progressively more prominent at the hila on the two lower frames, in keeping with normal vasculature at those levels rather than with parenchymal disease. No consolidation, mass, pleural fluid, or pneumothorax at any level. The airway is midline and non-deviated from trachea through the bifurcation to both main bronchi, which are patent and normally positioned with no visible intraluminal lesion or extrinsic compression. Mediastinal soft tissue is homogeneous with no discrete mass or clearly enlarged node; on the lowest frame the broad central soft-tissue density corresponds to heart and great vessels, undifferentiated because the study is unenhanced. On an unenhanced study nodes and unopacified vessels are isodense and cannot be separated, so the subcarinal and hilar nodal stations in particular are not assessable. A rounded left paravertebral contour is consistent with the descending thoracic aorta in normal position on the lower frames. Sternum, ribs, scapulae, and thoracic vertebrae appear intact with no fracture or lytic or sclerotic lesion. Chest wall soft tissues are mildly bulkier on the left than the right across all three frames, consistently enough to read as habitus or positioning rather than a focal abnormality. No discrete abnormality recorded at any of the three levels.
